checks.reason: Salesforce docs describe per-user OAuth 2.0 (with PKCE) via External Client Apps / Connected Apps as the authorization path for API and MCP clients.
API access is enabled by default in Developer Edition orgs, and Developer Edition is a free self-serve signup.
REST API is the primary documented integration surface; SOAP, GraphQL and Pub/Sub (gRPC) exist alongside it.
Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers are documented on developer.salesforce.com and hosted by Salesforce (forcedotcom/mcp-hosted repo says they are GA).
Buildable on a free Developer Edition, but customer orgs on Professional Edition need an API add-on and each org must enable/authorize the external client app, so caveats apply.
Multi-account (marketplace/private distribution) apps use OAuth; static-token apps are limited to one account.
Standard accounts can be free and developer test accounts are free HubSpot accounts (with a 90-day Enterprise-feature trial), so credentials are obtainable at $0.
API reference shows resource-oriented HTTP endpoints such as GET /crm/objects/.../contacts on api.hubapi.com.
HubSpot documents a publicly hosted remote MCP server at https://mcp.hubspot.com using OAuth.
Self-serve build/test works, but unlisted marketplace OAuth apps are capped at 25 installs until reviewed and listed, and some APIs need paid hubs.

Twenty's OAuth page maps 'External app acting on behalf of a user' to OAuth Authorization Code (with dynamic client registration) and reserves API keys for 'Internal scripts, automation'; API keys remain supported as a fallback.
Cloud has no free plan (30-day no-card trial), but 'Self-hosting the open source core is free', giving $0 working credentials; borderline with self_serve_trial if only Cloud is considered.
Docs state the Core and Metadata APIs are both available as REST and GraphQL.
Docs say 'Twenty exposes an MCP server' at https://{workspace}/mcp for Cloud and self-hosted, with OAuth or API key.
Self-serve Cloud trial and free self-hosting allow building and testing today with no review gate.
API v2 authentication section: use your personal API key via HTTP Basic (apikey:X); no OAuth flow is documented.
Pricing lists only paid plans (Growth/Pro/Enterprise) plus a 14-day trial of the Enterprise plan; no free plan.
Freshdesk API v2 is a REST/JSON API.
Freshworks documents its own MCP server at https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp (API-key auth), GA from September 10, 2026, on Growth/Pro/Enterprise.
Buildable via a self-serve trial, but continued testing requires a paid plan after 14 days.
'OAuth is required for public integrations available to all Front customers unless you obtain an exception from us.'
A free development account is self-serve, but apps are private to their instance until published, and publishing requires Front to test and technically approve the integration.
Front's Core API is a REST API accessed with OAuth or API tokens.
Front documents its own MCP server at https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp with OAuth via app.frontapp.com.
Buildable on a free dev account, but multi-customer distribution needs publishing/approval and OAuth must be authorized by company admins.
'Gladly API uses token-based Basic Authentication' with agent email as username and API token as password.
Tokens are created inside a customer's Gladly org by users granted the API User role by a Gladly admin; gladly.com offers only 'Get a demo'/contact sales, no self-serve signup.
Gladly publishes a REST API reference.

Gladly's help center (published 2026-11-18) documents the 'Gladly MCP for Claude' connector plus plugin at github.com/gladly/claude-plugin; scoped to Gladly AI (Guides, Workflows, sessions) and must be enabled per org by Gladly.
API is usable once inside a customer org (sandbox env at {org}.gladly.qa exists), so the enterprise-customer gate limits testing rather than fully blocking it.
Requests use HTTP Basic with API key SID/secret (default) or Account SID/Auth Token.
'Trial accounts expire 30 days after sign-up'; afterwards you must upgrade to keep building.
'Twilio APIs use standard RESTful HTTP methods to perform actions on resources.'
Twilio hosts a docs MCP at mcp.twilio.com/docs (Public Beta, no account actions), and its twilio-labs GitHub org publishes @twilio-alpha/mcp exposing Twilio APIs.
Self-serve trial credentials allow building and testing immediately; trial limits (30 days, verified recipients) are not an approval gate.
OAuth is the method for apps serving multiple Aircall customers; Basic api_id:api_token is for a company's own account.
OAuth credentials come from the Tech Partner program ('apply to the Tech Partner program'); only own-account Basic keys are available via a customer/trial account.
Aircall Public API is a REST API at api.aircall.io/v1.
Aircall's MCP FAQ says it does not offer an MCP server yet; existing Aircall MCP servers are third-party (e.g. themobilefirstco, StackOne).
API access is on all plans and a free test period exists for Basic-key testing, but OAuth distribution requires Tech Partner status.
API key/secret (Basic) is accepted by 19 of 25 listed APIs (Accounts, Numbers, SMS, Messages, Verify2...); Vonage recommends JWT for most use-cases and Voice/Video require JWT.
Signup gives €2 free credit with test-number restrictions and no stated time limit, so credentials are obtainable at $0.
Vonage APIs are HTTP REST APIs authenticated via Authorization header.
Vonage publishes a hosted Documentation MCP and the @vonage/vonage-mcp-server-api-bindings tooling server (balance, sms, numbers), documented on developer.vonage.com.
Self-serve free credit lets a toolkit be built and tested today; demo-mode limits only restrict destinations.
Access uses OAuth client or service account of a Google Cloud project; developer tokens were sunset on September 9, 2026.
Enabling the API grants only Test access; production needs an Explorer application (automated review in most cases), and Basic/Standard need brand verification or manual audit.
'The Google Ads API can be called either using gRPC or REST'; official client libraries are gRPC-based.
Google's own googleads GitHub org publishes google-ads-mcp and Google's developer docs provide its integration guide.
Buildable against test accounts immediately, but production access requires an access-level application/review.
